snapshot.note: Each row is an open question that must be answered before a decision can be made. 'What we know' is grounded in verified official sources; 'what we don't know' is the gap. Suggestions describe how to discover the missing information. Nothing is inferred.

questions.question: Which verified, machine-readable sources will supply team strength, player stats and pace inputs for signal generation?
questions.what_we_know: NFL.com publishes official standings, stats, schedules and the weekly injury report (all VERIFIED here).
questions.what_we_dont_know: The exact machine-readable endpoints and refresh cadence, and whether they cover every needed stat (pace, efficiency, splits).
questions.decision_blocked: Cannot finalize the signal-input pipeline or the data-integrity gate (VG-1) scope.
questions.suggestion: Map each required input to a specific official NFL.com endpoint; record HTTP status, retrieved timestamp and SHA-256 per fetch, mirroring the existing official-source manifest pattern.

questions.question: What is the documented, reproducible model that combines verified inputs into an originated spread, total and probability?
questions.what_we_know: The six-step origination method is documented (game context → strength → injury → situational → originate → validate).
questions.what_we_dont_know: The model's exact equation, weights and calibration method; no originated line values exist yet (blank/UNVERIFIED).
questions.decision_blocked: Cannot produce or validate any originated line until the model is defined and reproducible.
questions.suggestion: Author a versioned model spec (equation + weights + calibration) and a unit test that reproduces a sample line from a frozen input snapshot before any line is published.

questions.question: What is the minimum sample size and the skill-vs-luck significance threshold a strategy must clear to be ranked?
questions.what_we_know: Validation gates VG-2 (sample) and VG-3 (skill vs. luck) are defined as concepts; Brier score, log loss and significance testing are the chosen metrics.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The exact numeric thresholds (minimum bets, significance level, variance-explained cutoff).
questions.decision_blocked: Cannot accept any strategy to the leaderboard or award rewards without concrete thresholds.
questions.suggestion: Set and document numeric thresholds (e.g. minimum settled bets, p-value, variance fraction) and back-test them against a no-skill baseline before adopting.

questions.question: How are inter-leg and same-game correlations measured and what is the correlation cap for parlays and prop combos?
questions.what_we_know: Correlation handling is defined per strategy (S4, S5, S8); VG-4 enforces a correlation cap.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The correlation values themselves and the numeric cap; no correlation values are published (blank/UNVERIFIED).
questions.decision_blocked: Cannot build S4/S5/S8 or enforce VG-4 without measured correlations and a cap.
questions.suggestion: Compute historical inter-leg correlations from a frozen verified dataset, publish the values, and set the cap from the measured distribution.

questions.question: Which official source confirms the depth order (starter / 2nd / 3rd / 4th string) so a backup-replacing-starter deficiency can be verified?
questions.what_we_know: The NFL.com injury report is VERIFIED for player, position, injury, practice and game status; deficiency notes are ANALYSIS.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The depth-order / string designation for each player; the injury report alone does not state who is the 2nd/3rd/4th string.
questions.decision_blocked: Cannot verify the 'backup replacing starter' deficiency (the depth_string column stays UNVERIFIED).
questions.suggestion: Pull the official depth chart per team (NFL.com / team sites), record the depth order per position, and cross-check the injured player's string before marking a deficiency VERIFIED.

questions.question: What rewards and tiers are offered, and over what evaluation window is the leaderboard computed?
questions.what_we_know: Three reward tiers and six metrics are documented as a framework.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The concrete reward values, the competition window (weekly / season), and the tie-break rules.
questions.decision_blocked: Cannot finalize the leaderboard or publish rankings/rewards.
questions.suggestion: Define the reward values, evaluation window and tie-breaks; publish them on the leaderboard page before any strategy is ranked.

questions.question: Is any official league source for betting lines, odds or player props available, or must the model be self-originated with no market reference?
questions.what_we_know: No official league source publishes betting lines, odds or props; sportsbook lines are not official league values and are not used as VERIFIED inputs.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Whether the project will use a documented non-official market reference at all (clearly labelled non-official) or go fully model-originated.
questions.decision_blocked: Determines whether 'edge vs. market' can be computed or whether lines are compared only against the model's own baseline.
questions.suggestion: Decide and document the market-reference policy; if a non-official reference is used, label it clearly and keep it out of the VERIFIED official-source gate.

questions.question: Which leagues/seasons and bet types are in scope for the leaderboard competition?
questions.what_we_know: The current verified snapshot is NFL Week 10, 2026; strategy types span single bet, parlay and player props.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Whether the competition is NFL-only, which seasons count, and whether preseason/postseason are included.
questions.decision_blocked: Cannot define the leaderboard's data universe or the sample-size gate scope.
questions.suggestion: Confirm scope (NFL regular season only, or all NFL rows) and publish it on the leaderboard page.
